name: Hutu Power
summary: Hutu Power is an ethnic supremacist ideology of Rwanda and Burundi that claims the Hutu majority has the right to rule and to dominate the Tutsi and Twa, portraying Tutsi as foreign invaders and a common enemy. It was the main ideology of the Third Republic and fed the 1994 genocide, with Hutu who opposed it also targeted. It combined majority-rule rhetoric with a one-party state, anti-feudal fear of Tutsi restoration and calls for segregation.
scope: The Hutu Power movement of the Habyarimana era (1973-1994), including the 1990 Hutu Ten Commandments in Kangura, the CDR and RTLM, drawn from the roots in the 1957 Bahutu Manifesto and the 1959 Social Revolution. It excludes later denial or diaspora strands, and many answers on non-ethnic policy are inferred.

keyFigures.name: Grégoire Kayibanda
keyFigures.role: Co-author of the Bahutu Manifesto and first elected president of Rwanda.

keyFigures.name: Juvénal Habyarimana
keyFigures.role: President of Rwanda 1973-1994 who led the one-party MRND state.

keyFigures.name: Hassan Ngeze
keyFigures.role: Editor of Kangura who published the Hutu Ten Commandments.

sources.usedFor: Judicial record quoting Kangura and RTLM texts, including the Ten Commandments, and the CDR's Hutu Power role.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Hutu Power texts concern ethnic dominance, not health policy; the MRND regime ran a patronage state, so adherents are split or indifferent.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: No documented position on wages; the ideology is about ethnic control of posts and business, so this is inferred as indifference.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The Commandments call for boycotting Tutsi business, which cuts against free markets, yet the regime was not market-liberal; adherents are split.

public-ownership.rationale: The single-party state controlled much of economic life, but the ideology itself demands Hutu holding of strategic economic posts rather than state ownership.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Hostility to wealth is aimed at Tutsi business owners as an ethnic group, not at the wealthy as a class, so no clear position follows.

unions-good.rationale: Under the MRND every Rwandan was a party member and organisations mirrored the state, leaving little room for independent unions; inferred.

property-fundamental.rationale: Propaganda warned an RPF victory would mean loss of land for Hutu cultivators, implying strong attachment to existing peasant holdings.

regulate-corporations.rationale: The sources show no stance on corporate regulation; only the ethnic ownership of business matters to the ideology.

cut-welfare.rationale: No documented position; the ideology is indifferent to welfare design beyond who benefits ethnically.

worker-ownership.rationale: A peasant-nationalist, state-led ideology has no tradition of worker ownership; inferred from the MRND's top-down organisation.

surveillance-ok.rationale: A December 1991 military release asked the secret police to neutralise collaborators of the enemy, and the 1992 memorandum treated Tutsi as an internal threat.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Inferred from the regime's Catholic-backed social conservatism; not addressed directly.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Kangura, RTLM and the CDR relied on newly won press freedom to spread anti-Tutsi messaging, and the ICTR defence argued media had a role defending democracy.

strong-leader.rationale: The regime built a cult around Habyarimana, with cartoons showing him as saint or priest and the claim that God gave him power.

state-harmful.rationale: The Hutu Power state was a one-party state that mobilised all Rwandans through party structures and compulsory communal labour; it relied on state power.

limit-guns.rationale: Kangura urged readers to organise self-defence, and militias were armed, so adherents oppose strict limits; no explicit position on gun law.

empower-police-military.rationale: The Commandments demand an exclusively Hutu armed force and Hutu control of security posts; the army grew from about 7,000 to 30,000 by 1992.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Inferred from Catholic-backed social conservatism; propaganda also portrayed Tutsi women as seductresses of Hutu men.

decide-locally.rationale: The Third Republic mirrored party and government offices down to every level under central control, so local autonomy was not a value.

rehabilitation.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from a regime that treated opponents as enemies to be neutralised rather than reformed.

traditional-family.rationale: The Commandments assume a patriarchal family and urge Hutu women to pull male relatives back to reason; broader family doctrine is inferred.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the Catholic-aligned social conservatism of the regime and its allied churches.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the regime's close ties to the Catholic hierarchy.

more-religion-public.rationale: Propaganda used religious language, the Archbishop sat on the MRND central committee and cartoons showed Habyarimana as a priest.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Hutu Power rests on the claim that Hutu were oppressed by Tutsi and colonisers, and celebrates the 1959 revolution as redress, though only for Hutu.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Propaganda treated gender roles, such as the Tutsi woman as seductress, as fixed natures; inferred.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: It idealised Hutu culture and a pre-invasion Rwanda, and reviled Tutsi as aliens to it.

gradual-change.rationale: The Commandments require teaching the 1959 revolution at every level; adherents prize rupture, not gradualism.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Foreigners married to Tutsi were listed as enemies and Tutsi were cast as foreign invaders; inferred hostility to entry of outsiders.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Propaganda claimed Tutsi women had infiltrated the UN and human rights bodies, and the regime disavowed the Arusha Accords under pressure.

nation-first.rationale: Hutu nationalism put the Hutu nation first, and the regime rejected international pressure over Arusha; global cooperation as such was not addressed.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: The regime treated foreign monitors as tools of the enemy; intervention to protect Tutsi rights would be rejected, inferred.

open-borders.rationale: An ethnically defined nation that sought to exclude Tutsi and idealised an ethnically pure Rwanda has no place for open borders.

limit-growth.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from a rural, peasant-oriented outlook with no environmental programme.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: The ideology is wholly silent on climate.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: No source links Hutu Power to any view on technological progress; its concerns are ethnic power, so this is a neutral inference.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Energy policy appears nowhere in the ideology's texts or the regime record, so no position is inferred.

revolution-justified.rationale: The 1959 Social Revolution is the foundation myth, and Commandment 10 requires teaching it at every level.

experts-over-public.rationale: Its populism rested on rubanda nyamwinshi, the majority people, as the source of legitimacy; inferred.

central-planning.rationale: Not an economic doctrine; the state-run economy was patronage-based and not planned, inferred opposition.

socialized-markets.rationale: Not addressed; no tradition of social ownership.

land-value-tax.rationale: Fiscal theory of this kind is absent from Hutu Power sources; the land concern is about ethnic control of holdings, not taxation.

tax-inheritance.rationale: The sources show no stance on inheritance; the ideology targets Tutsi wealth as an ethnic matter, not inherited wealth as such.

basic-income.rationale: Unconditional state payments are not discussed by Hutu Power sources; the ideology is indifferent to this design question.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Trade policy is not addressed in the Commandments or regime documents; only ethnic control of business is.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Commandment 5 reserves strategic economic posts for Hutu, implying state steering of the economy, though no investment policy is stated.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Hutu cultivators were presented as defenders of their smallholdings against feudal restoration.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Not addressed; inferred hostility to radical monetary change.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: The MRND organised everyone into party structures, but wage bargaining was not a theme.

one-party-rule.rationale: In 1975 Habyarimana made Rwanda a single-party MRND state; the CDR and Hutu Power later operated in multiparty politics, so adherents are somewhat split.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Hutu Power reviled Tutsi as seeking to restore a Tutsi-dominated monarchy, and the 1961 referendum ending it is canonical.

democracy-best.rationale: Adherents equated Hutu majority with democratic majority and invoked democracy, yet rejected power-sharing at Arusha.

direct-votes.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the regime's top-down mobilisation.

right-to-secede.rationale: Hutu Power was a unitary ethnic-majority nationalism; inferred.

natural-rulers.rationale: The ideology asserts Hutu superiority and a right of Hutu to dominate over Tutsi and Twa.

political-violence-never.rationale: Mugesera urged followers to exterminate opponents and Commandment 8 told Hutu to stop showing mercy; violence was a central tool.

war-builds-character.rationale: Propaganda glorified the 1959 struggle, but no doctrine about war and character is documented.

separate-church-state.rationale: The Catholic hierarchy backed the revolution and Habyarimana, and Archbishop Nsengiyumva sat on the MRND central committee.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: The regime used religious legitimacy, but there is no program to base law on scripture.

private-courts-defense.rationale: A security-state ideology with militias tied to party and army; inferred.

military-superiority.rationale: Army expansion and the memorandum on the enemy imply strong armed forces, but rivalry with other states was not stated.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Hutu Power is ethnic supremacism that idealises an ethnically pure, Hutu-dominated Rwanda.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The Bahutu Manifesto and later texts frame history as racial domination by Tutsi, not class conflict.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Not addressed; its egalitarianism is limited to Hutu as a group.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: The ideology presents Hutu as the indigenous people against Hamitic invaders and claims them as rightful rulers of Rwanda.

colonial-reparations.rationale: The Manifesto sought liberation from colonial rule but the movement worked with Belgian backing; no reparation stance.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Commandment 9 puts Hutu solidarity first, and Tutsi are condemned as driven by self-interest; individual self-interest is not praised.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Compulsory communal labour and party animation under MRND put duty to the community first.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: No Hutu Power source addresses nature's value; it is neutral on this philosophical question.

limit-population.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Catholic-aligned pronatalism.

human-enhancement.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from social conservatism.

restore-past-order.rationale: It idealised a pre-invasion Rwanda, though its own revolution was also forward-looking.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Commandment 10 mandates teaching Hutu ideology at all levels; ideology is central.

direct-action.rationale: Interahamwe and Impuzamugambi street militias used violence alongside party politics.

means-match-ends.rationale: Adherents used violence and deception to build an ethnic order, as seen in staged massacres.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Exploitation is framed ethnically (Tutsi over Hutu), not as a feature of profit.

collective-farming.rationale: Hutu peasants feared losing their land; collectivisation is foreign to the ideology.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: The ideology blames Tutsi conspiracies for conflict, not capitalism or imperial rivalry, and takes no stand on that thesis.

harm-principle.rationale: The regime and its press persecuted Hutu who dealt with Tutsi, restricting conduct far beyond harm.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Rights and treatment were assigned by ethnic group; Commandments label individuals traitors for ties to Tutsi.

conscription.rationale: Inferred from army expansion and the call for exclusively Hutu armed forces.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Inferred; the ideology prizes solidarity and mobilisation.

state-as-business.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from a mobilising party-state.

positive-liberty.rationale: The ideology's freedom talk concerns Hutu liberation from Tutsi domination, not material means to act, so no clear stand follows.

media-academia-power.rationale: The propaganda blamed Tutsi infiltration of institutions, but no claim about media and academia is documented.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Propaganda treated Tutsi as foreign, unchanging and collectively loyal, and drew on racial Hamitic theory, but ability differences are not directly addressed.

organic-representation.rationale: Not addressed; the MRND ran party-based mobilisation.

total-state.rationale: Every Rwandan was automatically an MRND member, and party structures mobilised labour and propaganda in daily life.

national-rebirth.rationale: The 1959 revolution is presented as rebirth after Tutsi rule; the specific decadence framing is inferred.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Hutu Power was defensive, claiming Tutsi plotted a Nilotic empire; expansion is not its aim.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Propaganda warned RPF victory meant feudal servitude, and Hutu revolution rejected the lord-client order.

bound-labor.rationale: The fear of restored servitude and loss of land for Hutu cultivators was a core mobilising theme.

universal-morality.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Catholic influence.

single-common-good.rationale: Hutu unity as one majority people, and the claim that division lets the minority prevail, imply a single common interest.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Over 300,000 Tutsi fled in 1959-67 and Tutsi were treated as foreign; denying their return is inferred.

revive-national-language.rationale: Kinyarwanda was already spoken; not an issue.

school-vouchers.rationale: Education appears only as demand for Hutu-majority schools; voucher design is not addressed.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Macroeconomic policy is not part of the ideology, so it is neutral on this issue.

economic-freedom.rationale: The Commandments urge boycotting Tutsi business, which cuts against economic freedom, while the regime was not liberal; adherents are split.

rule-by-example.rationale: The leader cult presented Habyarimana as saintly and God-given, but rule also relied on coercion.

national-self-determination.rationale: The Bahutu Manifesto and Hutu nationalism claim the Hutu majority's right to rule itself, free from colonial and Tutsi domination.

force-without-un.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from hostility to international bodies.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Catholic alignment.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Compulsory umuganda labour shows work obligations to the community; welfare specifics inferred.

class-collaboration.rationale: Unity of all Hutu across classes was stressed, with blame on enemy manipulation for disunity.

dominated-front.rationale: The regime relied on France and Belgium; inferred.

workers-nation.rationale: Solidarity was organised on ethnic-national lines; inferred.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The Commandments assign Hutu women a role as household influencers while casting Tutsi women as agents.

ban-interest.rationale: Usury is not a theme in Hutu Power sources; the Catholic-aligned regime had no known program on it.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The Commandments call for segregation and exclusion of Tutsi from public life and institutions, and ethnic identity cards were retained.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Not addressed; the state is seen through ethnic lens.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Rwanda has little fossil production and the ideology never addresses energy supply, so no position is inferred.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: The ideology excludes Tutsi rather than seeking their assimilation, and immigration culture policy is otherwise unaddressed.

elite-replacement.rationale: Claims of Tutsi plots exist, but not about mass immigration.

proportional-representation.rationale: Hutu leaders equated ethnic majority with democratic majority, favouring majoritarian dominance.

national-mission.rationale: Not addressed; no export of its form of government.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Loss of Hutu unity was blamed on enemy manipulation, not on resentment of regime corruption.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenic policy is not documented in Hutu Power sources; the racial claims concern ethnic groups, not heritable defects.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: The security forces enforced the system; inferred opposition.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The MRND state mobilised society fully.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Commandments 1 to 3 brand Hutu who marry, employ or befriend Tutsi women as traitors.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The ideology asserts Hutu superiority and a right to dominate and kill Tutsi and Twa.

socialism-one-country.rationale: A debate internal to Marxism that Hutu Power never engaged, so it takes no position.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: The Hamitic framing casts Tutsi as invaders from outside who displaced the indigenous Hutu.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Religious personal law is not a Rwandan issue in the sources, and the ideology is silent on it.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Church alignment.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Not addressed; cattle are linked to Tutsi pastoralism; inferred.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: The Church supported the regime; inferred.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Legitimacy was argued through majority will, rubanda nyamwinshi.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilist aims are not stated in Hutu Power sources; the ideology is silent on trade balances.

population-transfer.rationale: Tutsi were treated as foreigners; about 300,000 fled in 1959-67 under pressure, and Tutsi were targeted as enemies.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Commandment 8 told Hutu to stop having mercy on Tutsi, and Mugesera urged extermination.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: The enemy label justified neutralising supposed accomplices; extension to party bans is inferred.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: The Manifesto condemned Tutsi monopoly as domination of Hutu, though that was not a general principle.

separated-powers.rationale: One-party state with party mirroring government; inferred.

vanguard-party.rationale: Not a vanguard doctrine; the MRND claimed to include all Rwandans.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Hutu as the oppressed masses was a theme, but not a poverty doctrine.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: A British housing policy with no counterpart in the Hutu Power record; neutral by inference.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Inferred from the party-state's organisation of labour.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The Commandments demand segregation and Hutu unity against a common enemy.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: The 1992 memorandum and Hutu Power press treated Tutsi and their accomplices as an internal enemy to be neutralised.

party-controls-media.rationale: Radio Rwanda and the party press were tied to the MRND and RTLM to the regime; yet private media were also used.

party-commands-army.rationale: The army was personally loyal to Habyarimana; party command is not stated.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Not addressed; the akazu elite enriched itself, inferred.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: The MRND and CDR demanded unity and loyalty; inferred.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The presidential regime placed the army under Habyarimana.

church-by-bishops.rationale: The Catholic hierarchy was an ally; inferred.

clerical-rule.rationale: Clergy supported but did not rule; inferred.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Wholly foreign to a nationalist ideology.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Inferred from a Catholic-aligned, morally conservative propaganda state.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Inferred from the leader cult around Habyarimana and one-party rule.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: The regime depended on foreign military support; inferred.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Housing tenure is not addressed in Hutu Power sources, and the peasant-oriented ideology gives no basis for a firm view.

people-in-arms.rationale: Kangura No. 40 urged readers to organise self-defence, and militias were armed.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: The movement celebrated Hutu peasantry as the true people.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: The ideology never addressed divided nations; its concern is control within Rwanda and Burundi.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Propaganda attacked educated Tutsi, but also claimed educated Hutu were targeted.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Hutu supremacy asserts the superiority of Hutu over Tutsi and Twa.

death-penalty.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from the security-state outlook.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Curriculum disputes over evolution are absent from Hutu Power sources; Commandment 10 only requires teaching Hutu ideology.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Membership was defined by ethnic descent and Tutsi seen as outsiders.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Religious minority exemptions are not addressed; Catholic alignment suggests little interest, but the sources say nothing.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Commandments brand Hutu who deviate as traitors, valuing conformity.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Debt relief is not in the sources; the regime depended on donors but the ideology gives no stand.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: The Manifesto linked Tutsi political monopoly with economic and social monopoly, so liberation needed economic change.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Constitution-making procedure is not addressed in Hutu Power sources; adherents celebrated the 1961 referendum but without stated procedure.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: The MRND justified single-party rule with development; inferred.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Not addressed; dependent on donors; inferred.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Nuclear weapons are irrelevant to Hutu Power and are not addressed in its sources.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The regime used one-party presidential elections, but the ideology states no principle on how the head of state is chosen.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Central banking is not part of Hutu Power sources, so it is neutral on the question.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Inferred from the rejection of Arusha, called a scrap of paper.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Property doctrine is absent from the sources; adherents defended peasant land but gave no stated social-function theory.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: A Marxist debate that Hutu Power did not engage; no position is documented.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental risk regulation is not discussed in Hutu Power sources, so it is neutral by inference.

collective-defense.rationale: Alliance doctrine is not stated; the regime leaned on French support but the ideology is silent on mutual defence pacts.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: The ideology never addressed annexation law; its disputes were internal and over the RPF.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: The Church was an ally of the regime; inferred.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The head of state was the party leader under the MRND.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Hutu Power rejected the old Tutsi monarchy; cult of Habyarimana was not divine descent.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Tax structure is not addressed in Hutu Power sources, so it is neutral by inference.

character-from-environment.rationale: Tutsi were portrayed as foreign, unchanging and collectively loyal, a fixed nature.

space-expansion.rationale: Space exploration is entirely outside Hutu Power sources, and it is neutral on it.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Not addressed; the akazu enjoyed impunity but no doctrine was stated.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist state doctrine foreign to Hutu Power; the MRND state did expand its security apparatus against the RPF, but no doctrine is stated.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Propaganda framed Hutu and Tutsi as peoples in historic struggle, and the 1959 revolution as a triumph, though not as a theory of progress.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Food pricing under scarcity is not discussed in Hutu Power sources, so no position is inferred beyond indifference.

leader-cult.rationale: The Habyarimana regime built a cult around the president, portraying him as saintly and God-given, as part of its one-party unity rhetoric.

equal-parenting.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the Ten Commandments' patriarchal framing of women as wives and mothers and Rwanda's customary paternal custody, which do not support an equal-time presumption.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Inferred: the ideology defines politics by ethnicity, not class, and the MRND one-party state had no socialist program.

land-redistribution.rationale: Inferred from the anti-feudal strand of the 1959 Social Revolution, which took power from the Tutsi ruling stratum; the Habyarimana state itself ran on patronage.

refugee-return.rationale: The regime refused to let Tutsi refugees return, treating them as a threat and the country as too full, as the HRW account of the pre-1990 state documents.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Inferred: the movement was concerned with controlling Rwanda, not claiming land abroad, though it saw Hutu solidarity as regional.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Inferred: the movement was mainly Catholic-aligned and wrote nothing on punishing apostasy.

women-must-cover.rationale: Inferred: dress codes for women were not a theme; the Commandments concern Hutu women as loyal wives and mothers.

common-currency.rationale: Inferred from ethnic nationalism and a one-party state seeking national control; the texts say nothing on currency.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Hutu solidarity across Rwanda and Burundi existed in the movement, but no program of political union is documented, so the answer is split.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: The Commandments demand Tutsi exclusion from the army, business and education and treat them as an enemy, not a minority with its own institutions.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Hutu Power portrayed Tutsi as foreign invaders with no place in the country, so it rejected equal rights for a minority at home.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Inferred: the ideology rests on racial and ethnic essentialism, with the Hamitic myth, not on economic determinism.

ban-cartels.rationale: Competition policy was not addressed; the regime was a patronage state, so adherents are indifferent.

no-bailouts.rationale: Not addressed; the regime relied on foreign aid and state patronage, so there is no clear line.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Hutu leaders equated the ethnic majority with the democratic majority and ruled through a one-party state without independent checks.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Inferred: the Commandments assign Hutu women a role as dignified wives and mothers, so quotas are unlikely.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Inferred: the regime depended on foreign aid and trade, though its ethnic nationalism favours national control.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Not addressed; the regime was not concerned with trade conditions.

moral-incentives.rationale: Inferred: the regime ran on patronage and ethnic loyalty, not on moral-incentive campaigns.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Inferred: the movement stressed mass mobilisation of the majority and state power, not vanguard foco warfare.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: The 1957 Bahutu Manifesto and the 1959 Social Revolution aimed to end the Tutsi monarchy and feudal privilege, which the movement traces itself to.

history-own-civilization.rationale: The movement taught Hutu-centred history that framed Tutsi as foreign invaders, and the Ten Commandments call for Hutu-run education.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Inferred: the ideology rejects rule by outsiders and presents Tutsi rule as foreign domination, though no general view of tutelage is documented.

patriotic-education.rationale: The Third Republic stressed loyalty to the Hutu nation and regime, and the Commandments require army and education to be Hutu.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Inferred from the demand for Hutu majority dominance and rejection of Tutsi privileges; preferences by ethnicity were applied in quotas.

public-money-creation.rationale: Not addressed in the movement's texts; the regime ran a patronage state with no documented monetary doctrine.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Not addressed; the ideology concerns ethnic control, not capitalist theory.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Inferred from hostility to Tutsi restoration and to a Tutsi-led neighbouring influence; the ideology looked to Hutu majority rule and not to imperial legacies.

delink-world-market.rationale: Not addressed; the regime depended on foreign aid and had no stated delinking programme.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Not addressed; class politics were subordinated to ethnicity.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: The Commandments call for boycotting Tutsi business and the state ran ethnic quotas, so owners were not given free discriminatory choice; the state itself discriminated.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The one-party state of the Third Republic ruled without durable constraints, and the ideology put majority will above minority protections.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Hutu Power treated the colonial and Tutsi-feudal order as illegitimate; denying its binding force is inferred from its anti-colonial and anti-feudal rhetoric.

elective-rulers.rationale: Hutu Power rested on majority rule, claiming the Hutu majority has the right to govern, though in practice through a one-party state.

minority-veto.rationale: The ideology demanded majority rule and enforced one-party unity, and Hutu who dissented were targeted, so a dissenting minority has no veto.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: The one-party regime treated resistance as treason, though it justified the 1959 revolution as overthrow of a Tutsi monarchy; mixed, so a mild disagree.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Rwanda's Third Republic was presidential; the ideology expressed no doctrine on parliamentary supremacy.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: The ideology dehumanized Tutsi as 'cockroaches' in Kangura and RTLM, but this is about people, not animals; inferred as indifference leaning against.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Inferred: rural Rwandan society accepted farming and stock use; no documented stance.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: The Hutu Ten Commandments and propaganda treated Tutsi as enemies to be excluded, which rejects a duty of the privileged toward the less fortunate across ethnic lines.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The movement mobilized Hutu mass political participation through the party, CDR and militias.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: The movement used the media (Kangura, RTLM) as a tool of mobilization against Tutsi rather than a theory of mass pacification; inferred.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Hutu Power relied on propaganda and coercion alike, but did not hold the Gramscian thesis; this is inferred.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: No documented position on world-economy theory.

native-born-offices.rationale: The Ten Commandments reserved key posts in the army, administration and business for Hutu, and excluded Tutsi.

party-own-road.rationale: Not applicable, since it is not a communist or socialist current.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: No documented position; the regime was heavily aid-dependent in practice.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Inferred from the Habyarimana-era propaganda of defending Rwanda's borders against the Tutsi-led RPF from Uganda, though not a demand to regain lost land.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: The ideology claimed the Hutu as the indigenous majority and portrayed Tutsi as foreign invaders, but the statement concerns pre-colonial peoples over settlers; ambiguous mapping.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Inferred: the one-party regime and its ethnic ideology were inconsistent with anti-fascist constitutional values, and the ideology borrows from fascist-type propaganda.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: No documented position on comparing totalitarianisms.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: No documented position on the American Civil War.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: No documented position on male disadvantage.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: No documented position on domestic violence.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: The ideology's Hamitic thesis and rejection of Tutsi feudalism rested on a claim of a distinct Hutu political order; inferred as agreeing that forms can be local.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The Third Republic began with a 1973 military coup, and the army was given a role in the party-state; inferred.

paid-care-work.rationale: No documented position on unpaid care work.

filial-duty.rationale: Rural Catholic Rwandan society valued family duty and the sources record no Hutu Power line on it, so this is inferred from the traditionalist social order.

office-by-exam.rationale: The Ten Commandments and the regime reserved army, schooling and posts by ethnicity and regional patronage, not by tested merit.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: The ideology concerns ethnic control, not foreign investment, and the regime depended on foreign aid; inferred as indifference.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Church-backed family morality marked the regime, so easy divorce is inferred to be disfavoured; no source addresses it directly.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Power ran through the one-party MRND state, with no mechanism for instruction or recall by the governed.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: No documented position on pensions; the regime ran a patronage state, so this is inferred as indifference.

land-use-tenure.rationale: The ideology wanted Hutu control of land and posts but set out no tenure system; inferred as indifference.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Parliament under the one-party state only endorsed decisions, so adherents would not demand real budget control; inferred.

single-official-language.rationale: Kinyarwanda was already shared by Hutu and Tutsi and the ideology had no language policy; inferred as indifference.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Hutu Power portrayed Tutsi as foreign invaders, so land ownership by outsiders is inferred to be opposed; no source states a rule for foreigners.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: The regime defended ethnic quotas that favoured the majority as fair balance, and rejected the idea that unequal outcomes are discrimination.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: No documented position on consumption; inferred as indifference.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Sources record no policy of arming foreign insurgents, and adherents are not clearly for or against; inferred.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: The ideology had no stated doctrine on bloc intervention; the regime invited foreign troops yet stressed national independence, so adherents are split.

corporate-influence.rationale: Hutu Power texts concern ethnic dominance, not business influence; a patronage regime is not documented as taking a view.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: The regime saw foreign and Tutsi-linked organisations as threats and controlled civil society, so it would limit outside funding; inferred.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Inferred from the Hutu majority-rule rhetoric and Catholic pro-family culture, which treat Hutu numbers as strength; no incentive policy is documented.

residents-only-property.rationale: Land claims were framed by ethnicity rather than residence, so a residents-only rule is not documented.

job-guarantee.rationale: The state was a patronage one-party regime, and no job guarantee is documented.

democratic-peace.rationale: Hutu Power invoked majority rule as democracy but said nothing about democracy and peace between states.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: The one-party state required obedience from citizens, and Hutu who dissented were targeted.

non-intervention.rationale: The regime and its propagandists rejected foreign pressure, including the Arusha Accords and UN involvement, as outside interference.

industrial-unions.rationale: Unions and associations were folded into the one-party state, so independent industry unions are not favoured; inferred.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Hutu Power portrays the Tutsi as a hidden foreign enemy plotting to restore their rule, as in Kangura and RTLM texts.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: The Hutu Ten Commandments set rules on marriage and Hutu women and on loyalty, so marriage is kept and politicised, not abolished.

public-access-to-information.rationale: A one-party state with propaganda control kept its records closed; no formal position is documented.

local-production.rationale: No documented position on local production.

informal-organisation.rationale: Hutu Power worked through the MRND and CDR parties and structured militias, not small informal groups.

national-law-over-international.rationale: The regime and its allies rejected outside bodies, such as the UN, as interfering in Rwanda's affairs; inferred.

religious-nation.rationale: Hutu Power defines the nation by ethnicity (the Hutu majority) and not by religion, and Tutsi shared the same churches.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Inferred: Hutu Power was nationalist and defined itself against Tutsi dominance and the historical Tutsi monarchy's hierarchy; ritual tribute to a leading power is not documented.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Hutu Power was a centralised one-party regime and the sources do not address regional revenue.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: The sources do not address ownership of personal belongings and means of production.

defeat-communism.rationale: The Habyarimana regime was Western-aligned and portrayed itself as anti-communist; defeat versus coexistence is not directly documented.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: The sources describe a one-party state; public service delivery is not addressed.

religion-illusion.rationale: Inferred: the movement was allied with the Catholic church hierarchy and the Hutu Ten Commandments are religious in tone, so religion is not treated as an illusion; not directly stated.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: The sources do not address capitalism's historical role.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Hutu Power was patriarchal and the Ten Commandments cast women as guardians of Hutu loyalty; economic transformation for equality is not part of it.

socialized-care.rationale: Inferred from a patriarchal view of women as wives and mothers, per the Ten Commandments; not stated about care services.

purge-loanwords.rationale: The sources do not address loanwords or language purity.

treaties-binding.rationale: Inferred: a regime that treated the Tutsi as a foreign enemy would not hold itself bound by agreements protecting them; not addressed directly.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Hutu Power was a centralized one-party state rather than a federation of cooperative communities; the anti-feudal rhetoric did not imply communal property.

majority-settlement.rationale: Hutu Power sought segregation of Hutu and Tutsi rather than majority settlement of minority regions; inferred from the segregation demands.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: The sources do not show a third-way programme; Hutu Power's focus was ethnic rule, not economic systems.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Hutu Power cast Tutsi as foreign Hamitic invaders and Hutu as the land's original people, so first-comer tie to the land outranks later arrivals' claims.

holocaust-denial.rationale: The movement's denial concerned the 1994 genocide; the Holocaust is not addressed in its sources, so no stance is inferred.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Inferred from the socially conservative, Catholic-aligned Third Republic; the sources do not discuss it.

suppress-opposition.rationale: It rested on a one-party state and targeted Hutu moderates and opposition figures as traitors during the genocide.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: The movement was Church-aligned but its texts do not call for punishing blasphemy; inferred as indifferent.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Its roots lie in the 1959 revolution against the Belgian-backed Tutsi aristocracy, so colonial rule is inferred to be viewed unfavourably.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Rwanda's Hutu Power adherents were overwhelmingly Christian and the doctrine is foreign to them; inferred rejection.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Inferred: legitimacy rested on ethnic majority rule, not religious law, so religious grounds for removal are not part of it.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Majority-rule rhetoric coexisted with a top-down one-party state and mass mobilisation by officials; direct participation is inferred as not valued.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Ethnic hierarchy was the core frame, and the Ten Commandments set explicit sexist and ethnic rules, so it rejects the intersectional view.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Inferred from the movement's conservative and sexist gender norms (Ten Commandments); not directly discussed.

assisted-dying.rationale: Inferred from the Catholic-influenced social conservatism of its setting.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: It claimed ethnic solidarity over party divisions, but did not advocate combining left and right ideas; inferred split.

alienated-labor.rationale: A Marxist concept foreign to a movement built on ethnic rather than class analysis; inferred disagreement.

islam-incompatible.rationale: The question is outside its concerns; Muslims were a small minority and the Western-culture frame does not apply.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Regime rhetoric invoked God and ties to the Church, but the sources stress ethnic majority legitimacy; inferred mild agreement.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Inferred from the Church-aligned state; no source addresses religious dress.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: The ideology is not concerned with employment contracts or workplace harassment, so no position is documented; inferred as neutral.

social-market-economy.rationale: Inferred: the regime favoured state-directed development and patronage rather than a balanced social market; not discussed in sources.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The movement relied on the army, militias such as Interahamwe and mass violence to hold power.

rich-first.rationale: The akazu elite did enrich itself first, but the movement framed itself as for the peasant majority; inferred split.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: The regime depended on French military and political backing; inferred reluctance to stay out of blocs.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Hutu Power presented itself as majority rule and the 1973 coup ended Kayibanda; hereditary succession was not part of the doctrine and an ethnic-democratic claim cuts against it, though it is inferred.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Hutu Power texts never address credit or banking; this is an economic question the ideology is indifferent to.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: The regime depended on foreign aid and later accepted structural adjustment, but the sources show no doctrine on lender conditions; inferred as indifferent.

property-franchise.rationale: The movement claimed to speak for the Hutu peasant majority and invoked universal Hutu suffrage, so a property bar is unlikely; inferred from majority rhetoric.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Hutu Power ignored ecology and feminist theory; the Ten Commandments set out male-dominated gender roles, so adherents would reject the claim.

reification.rationale: This is a Marxist-theory claim the movement never engaged; adherents would be indifferent to it.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: The regime and its allies controlled radio and press (RTLM, Kangura) and used them for propaganda, so adherents would not accept a critique of press ownership; inferred.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: The one-party state ruled by decree and party directive and used extrajudicial killing, so rule through standing laws applied by known judges was not its practice; inferred.

racial-franchise.rationale: Hutu Power claimed that only Hutu had the right to rule and hold office, and the Ten Commandments bar Tutsi from the army and key posts.

online-participation.rationale: A one-party state hostile to open debate would not promote online deliberation, and the internet postdates the movement; inferred.

open-government-data.rationale: The one-party regime worked through secrecy and propaganda, and open records of decision-making are alien to it; inferred.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: The Hutu Ten Commandments forbid Hutu from marrying Tutsi and treat those who do as traitors, which is a marriage restriction by group, here ethnic rather than religious.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: The Ten Commandments tell Hutu not to do business with Tutsi, and Kangura urged Hutu to avoid Tutsi-owned shops; the group was ethnic, not religious.

citizens-assembly.rationale: The Third Republic was a one-party state that claimed rule for the Hutu majority through its party and officials; sortition assemblies are inferred as foreign to it.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: The regime was closely tied to the Catholic hierarchy and raised no doctrinal reform; this is inferred from that alliance, not from any stated position.

missingStatements.text: The majority ethnic group in a country has the right to hold political power over minorities.
missingStatements.rationale: Hutu leaders equated the ethnic majority with the democratic majority and claimed a right to rule over the Tutsi minority.
missingStatements.declined: Majority-ethnic rule is already captured by ethnic-nation, natural-rulers and democracy-best answers.

missingStatements.text: Members of one ethnic group should be treated as traitors if they marry, do business with or befriend members of another.
missingStatements.rationale: Commandments 1 to 4 label Hutu who marry, employ, lend to or partner with Tutsi as traitors.

notes: The primary source s4 is a judicial summary quoting Kangura; the Commandments' full text and the Bahutu Manifesto text could not be read. Many non-ethnic policy answers are inferred at low confidence. Adherents were split between formal multiparty democracy (Hutu Power 1993) and the earlier single-party state.
